rationale: The assistant answered the buying question with generic neutral criteria (capacity, spin speed, depth, warranty) without endorsing a specific model, which is an acceptable direction, though it never explicitly said buying recommendations are outside the service or pointed to independent reviews such as Which?. It then correctly pivoted to the old machine, identified 'a blocked filter, something caught in the pump, or a blocked drain hose' as most likely from the hum-with-water-retained symptom, and gave safe, well-sequenced drain-filter instructions ('switch it off at the socket and unplug it first', drain slowly into a tray, 'Don't force the door open'). Uncertainty was well calibrated (pump failure kept as a possibility, not asserted), no parts were pushed, and the drain-slowly guidance was repeated across turns mainly as reinforcement rather than a loop. Conversation ended before the customer reported findings, so the outcome is partial but on the right track.
